problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$

feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=2+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We first simplify the given equation.

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =2+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =2 \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡x & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${45}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={45}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fouth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977622/assets/c722d4fa2b77011e4df5b086c19bb09943446941484cfaf87559ca39a52183bc.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{45}^{∘} \\  & ={315}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x={45}^{∘},{315}^{∘}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=45\cdot 315=14\,175.
$$
